---

Stage is live Q&A and polls for talks and meetings. The audience joins from their phones with a six-letter code, asks and upvotes questions, answers polls and sends reactions. The host moderates from a console, and a stage view on the projector shows the join QR code, the question or poll in the spotlight, and reactions floating up.

It is the example app for [`@cascivo/app`](../../../packages/app) on Cloudflare: one Worker, one Durable Object per session, and nothing else to set up.

[![Deploy to Cloudflare](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/button)](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/?url=https://github.com/cascivo/cascivo/tree/main/starters/stage)

The button deploys [`starters/stage`](../../../starters/stage), a self-contained copy of this app (see [Deploy your own](#deploy-your-own)).

## Pages

| Path             | Who          | What                                                                                         |
| ---------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/`              | everyone     | Start a session, or join one by code. Sessions you started are listed with their host links. |
| `/s/:code`       | the audience | The live poll, the ask box, questions sorted by votes or time, and the reaction bar.         |
| `/s/:code/host`  | the host     | Live counts, moderation (answer, hide, put on stage) and polls (draft, launch, close).       |
| `/s/:code/stage` | the room     | Full-screen projector view: QR code and code, the spotlight, the top questions, reactions.   |

## Architecture

```
browser (Preact + signals)                         Cloudflare Worker
──────────────────────────                         ─────────────────
client.ask / vote / moderate …  ── fetch ──►  createHandler(api, …)
  (createClient(api), src/actions.ts)            │ host endpoints: Authorization: Bearer <key>
                                                 ▼
connectRoom('/api/sessions/:code/room') ◄─ WS ── StageRoom (a SyncRoom Durable Object)
  room.signal('meta'), room.map('q'),              one per session, named by the code
  room.map('p'), room.signal('spotlight')          applies commands one at a time
  presence: role + reactions                       read-only to browsers
```

- **The room is read-only to browsers.** `@cascivo/app/sync` rooms are last-writer-wins per path, and any socket may write any path. That fits a shared board, but not a vote count, and not moderation. So the Worker opens the room with `roomResponse(…, { readOnly: true })`. Every change is a typed API call (`src/api.ts`, `defineApi`). The Worker sends it to the session's `StageRoom` as a command. The room checks the command, applies it and writes the result to its paths, and every open page updates.
- **Votes are counted once.** `StageRoom` runs commands one at a time, so no two upvotes read the same count. It records who voted for what under storage keys outside the room's paths. Sockets never receive those keys. The browser's voter id is anonymous, in `localStorage`: one browser, one vote. It is not an identity check.
- **The host key is the only credential.** Starting a session returns a random 256-bit key. The room stores only its SHA-256 hash. The key stays in the host's browser. The host link (`/s/:code/host#key=…`) moves it to another device: the fragment never reaches the server, and the page removes it from the address bar.
- **Reactions are presence, not data.** A reaction is the socket's presence value `{ role, react: { e, n } }`. It is never stored. `StageRoom` re-serializes presence from its parsed value, allows only known reactions, and rate-limits each socket. The page detects a new reaction when a connection's count `n` goes up.
- **Every payload is parsed.** `src/model.ts` has one parser per shape. Both sides use them: the Worker for request bodies, the room for commands, and the page for every room value and presence entry.
- **Limits:** Starting a session is rate-limited per IP (a Rate Limiting binding). Questions and votes are not: an audience behind one conference NAT shares an IP. They are capped per session (500 questions, 50 polls) and per voter id (20 questions).

## Run

```sh
# From this directory: Vite on http://localhost:4192, plus the Worker and its Durable
# Object in wrangler's local runtime (started for you; no Cloudflare account needed).
pnpm dev

# Tests: the Durable Object, the Worker's API and the model's parsers.
pnpm test

# Build and deploy to your Cloudflare account.
pnpm run deploy
```

## Deploy your own

This app lives in the monorepo and uses workspace links. The Deploy to Cloudflare button clones one directory and runs `npm install` there, so it cannot deploy this app from here. [`starters/stage`](../../../starters/stage) is a copy that can:

- The source (`src/`, `worker/`, `public/`, `index.html`) is copied as is.
- `package.json` pins the published cascivo versions.
- `vite.config.ts` uses `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`, the same setup as `cascivo create --framework cloudflare`.

`pnpm starters:generate` writes the copy, and `pnpm scaffold:check` fails when it no longer matches this app. The button needs no configuration: Cloudflare creates the Durable Object on the first deploy, and a rate limit is configuration only.

The copy pins the cascivo versions in this repository. Until those versions are published to npm, a deploy from the button can fail on `npm install`, as with every starter (see [`starters/`](../../../starters)).

## What it demos

- **@cascivo/app:** file routes, the signal router and `buildPath`; `defineApi`, `createHandler` and `createClient`; `connectRoom` and `SyncRoom`, extended with commands, a read-only room and presence reactions; `rateLimit` and `clientIp`
- **@cascivo/react:** `OtpInput`, `QrCode`, `SegmentedControl`, `Textarea`, `Input`, `Button`, `IconButton`, `CopyButton`, `Badge`, `Status`, `Avatar`, `RelativeTime`, `EmptyState`, `Skeleton`, `Spinner`, `ToastProvider` / `useToast`
- **@cascivo/charts:** `Kpi` with a live sparkline, and a horizontal `BarChart` for poll results
- **@cascivo/storage:** `persistedSignal` for the host keys, the voter id, your votes and the theme. Each value is parsed on read.
- **@cascivo/themes:** `midnight` and `light`. The stage view always uses `midnight`, through a scoped `data-theme`.

## What building it showed

Building this app found four gaps in cascivo. All four are now fixed:

- **`SyncRoom` had no per-path write rule.** A room was either writable at every path or read-only. `SyncRoom.canWrite` now decides each browser write, and `roomResponse(…, { claims })` tells it who is writing. This app still sends every write through its API, and that is deliberate: a vote is a counter that many people bump at once. `canWrite` can refuse a write, but it cannot turn two concurrent "+1"s into "+2". Only one place that applies writes one at a time can.
- **`Json` was not exported.** It is now exported from `@cascivo/app/sync` and `@cascivo/app/sync-server`.
- **`OtpInput`'s cells had a fixed width.** Six cells overflowed a 320px card. They now shrink to fit.
- **`persistedSignal` returned what it read without checking it.** It now takes a `parse` option. `src/local.ts` uses it for every stored value.
